subject: Pipeline SLO triage: streaming + concurrency checks for p95/p99 qualification
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Cho <alex.cho@veridian.ai>, procurement@veridian.ai, s.reliability@veridian.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-05T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Pipeline SLO triage: streaming + concurrency checks for p95/p99 qualification

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment on business need and the target KPIs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone (internal + Veridian SRE/procurement) has a single source of truth.

High-level ask from Veridian: confirm hosted API feasibility for production rollout (user-facing LLM features) with the following near-term goals:
- p95 end-to-end <= 200 ms, p99 end-to-end <= 450 ms for text-generation paths under expected production traffic.
- Sustained throughput target: 120 requests/sec across peak region (US-East). Burst tolerance: up to 600 req/s for short windows (~60s).
- Concurrent active requests: up to 500 concurrent streaming sessions (chunked token streaming via SSE/websocket).
- Streaming requirement: first token within 120 ms, steady-state per-chunk latency <= 60 ms, support for 16–64 token chunks.

What Redwood will do next (proposed):
1) Run side-by-side qualification: run hosted test harness against Veridian traffic profile (we'll request sanitized traffic).
2) Provide an acceptance checklist (we attached streaming-checklist-v1.xlsx) with measurement methodology (client-side vs edge).
3) Deliver a short runbook summarizing load test plan and required artifacts from Veridian (API keys, traffic sample, SLA window) — attached as runbook-hosted-vs-incumbent.md.

What we need from Veridian (action items):
- Share a 48h sample of production traffic (kpi-traffic-profile.csv stub attached) and one representative trace for a slow user flow.
- Confirm whether p95/p99 measurements should be client-observed (user delta) or server-observed (edge only). We'll run both if helpful, but need confirmation for acceptance criteria.
- Give access to a staging API key and a contact for your SRE who can enable network-level traces (we copied s.reliability@veridian.ai).

Proposed timeline:
- Veridian shares artifacts by EOD 2027-05-07.
- Redwood runs qualification tests 05/08–05/10 and shares initial results by 05/11.
- Follow-up tech deep-dive (30–45m) the week of 05/12 to review traces and tuning.

Attachments referenced: streaming-checklist-v1.xlsx (measurement checklist), kpi-traffic-profile.csv (sample column-stub), runbook-hosted-vs-incumbent.md (planned harness & acceptance criteria).

Let me know if you'd like us to tighten the p95/p99 bounds in the acceptance criteria or shift the measurement to strictly client-observed. Next step: Alex — can you confirm timeline and who on your side will provide the traffic sample?

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(h) +1 415 555 0142 | hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: streaming-checklist-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), kpi-traffic-profile.csv (CSV)

From: Alex Cho <alex.cho@veridian.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>, procurement@veridian.ai, s.reliability@veridian.ai
Date: 2027-05-05T14:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pipeline SLO triage: streaming + concurrency checks for p95/p99 qualification

Appreciate the clear recap, Hannah — that maps to our expectations. A few clarifying questions from the engineering side before we produce the traffic sample: 

1) Measurement baseline: We typically measure end-to-end from the client (browser/mobile) so the p95/p99 goals are user-observed. We can provide both client-side and server-side traces, but official acceptance will likely be client-observed. Can you confirm Redwood's recommended default?

2) Burst profile: The 600 req/s burst — is that tied to any specific campaign or simulated user behavior? We have auto-scaling rules in our edge that may affect cold-starts; we'd like to capture that in the trace.

3) Streaming semantics: We use a websocket-based streaming path with 32-token chunks by default. Does Redwood need per-chunk timing or per-token? We can include both, but per-token timings are noisy.

Action items from Veridian side:
- I'll ask SRE (cc'd) to export a 72h sanitized trace with client timestamps and an edge trace with server timestamps. Expect delivery by COB 2027-05-07 if no blockers.
- Procurement: we'll confirm the NDA/PO cadence; I tagged procurement on this thread.

One note: our incumbent provider reports p95 around 220–260ms (client-observed) and p99 at ~560ms during large bursts. We'll want to see side-by-side numbers. Can Redwood confirm the instrumentation you will use so we can align?

I'll attach a small traffic sample (veridian-traffic-sample.csv) in my next email.

Best,
Alex Cho
Product Lead, Conversational AI
Veridian Health

Attachment stub: veridian-traffic-sample.csv (will follow with sanitized sample)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Cho <alex.cho@veridian.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-06T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pipeline SLO triage: streaming + concurrency checks for p95/p99 qualification

Thanks — quick technical plan and a proposed, concrete acceptance definition so the team can act when we get traces.

Measurement methodology recommendation:
- Run both client-observed and server-observed measurements. For acceptance we recommend client-observed p95 <= 220 ms, p99 <= 500 ms (we set slightly more conservative than your current incumbent numbers to reduce the risk of regressions). If Veridian insists on stricter bounds, we can iterate.

Streaming and chunking:
- We'll capture per-chunk latency (time from server send to client receive) and report a 50th/95th/99th distribution for chunk latency. Acceptance: median chunk <= 30 ms, p95 chunk <= 60 ms, p99 chunk <= 120 ms.

Concurrency and throughput:
- We'll simulate realistic concurrency with session-based streaming: 500 concurrent sessions sustained for 10 minutes, spike tests to 600 req/s for 60s windows.

Load test plan (what Redwood needs):
- Staging API key and an endpoint that mirrors production routing (or a redirect rule).
- Sample dataset: 10k–20k sanitized requests representative of distribution (short/long prompts, streaming vs non-streaming).
- Network topology note: capture both client (browser) timestamped traces and edge logs. If you can't provide client traces for PII reasons, server-side + synthetic client overlay is acceptable.

Acceptance criteria (pass/fail):
- Client-observed p95 <= 220 ms and p99 <= 500 ms across a 30-minute steady-state run at target throughput.
- Streaming chunk p95 <= 60 ms, and no more than 1% of chunks exceed 200 ms.
- No sustained error rate increase > 0.5% versus baseline; transient spikes must auto-heal within 90s.

We attached a short runbook (runbook-hosted-vs-incumbent.md) that details the test harness commands, the metric collection endpoints, and the dashboard links we'll populate. Once we have the traces, we'll schedule the side-by-side run and share a reproducible report.

I'll lead the test execution with Ben on monitoring and Laura on client-scripting. Hannah — can you confirm the window for the deep-dive after we post initial results?

- Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
